description: Flat 8 m square of coarse tropical grass worn through to bare earth in patches -- the verge and temple-ground surface, as one quad and one seamless PBR texture set.

image.prompt:
A SEAMLESSLY TILING TOP-DOWN GROUND TEXTURE. This is a flat material swatch, not a photograph of a scene or of an object. The camera looks straight down at the ground from directly overhead, perfectly orthographic, with no perspective, no horizon, no vanishing point and no tilt.

The surface: Flat square of coarse tropical lawn grass seen as a single unbroken surface viewed from above, thick blades in the healthy areas thinning to sparse tufts and worn through to bare reddish earth along the walked patches, edge to edge ground cover only, no kerb, no border, no bushes and no upright plants Materials: Seamlessly tiling coarse broad-bladed tropical grass in mixed greens from deep to sun-bleached yellow-green, thinning to sparse tufts and bare rust-red earth on the worn paths, dry brown thatch matted under the blades, scattered dry leaf litter and small stones, darker damp green in the shaded runs and scorched yellow patches in the open, a few flat weeds and clover clumps; the ground cover must wrap on all four edges with no distinctive tuft or bare patch repeating across a seam.

Scale: the square shown covers exactly 8 by 8 metres of real ground, so every stone, block, slab, joint, marking, rut and tuft in it is drawn at its true size relative to that. Do not zoom in on a detail and do not pull back to show a wider scene.

Tiling: the texture must repeat seamlessly on all four edges. What runs off the left edge continues onto the right edge, and what runs off the top continues onto the bottom, exactly. No feature may be cut in half at an edge without its other half appearing at the opposite edge. Laid out four by four this must read as one continuous surface with no visible grid, no repeated landmark feature and no seam.

Framing: the surface fills the entire frame edge to edge and corner to corner. There is no border, no frame, no margin, no backdrop, no background, no matte and no empty space of any kind. The ground continues past every edge of the image.

Nothing stands on it and nothing bounds it: no kerb, no wall, no step, no gutter, no drain, no manhole cover, no grass verge, no plants, no people, no vehicles, no furniture, no objects, no litter, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows.

Lighting: flat, even, shadowless overhead illumination, like a lightbox. The image is the surface's true albedo. No sun, no cast shadows, no directional highlights, no specular blowout, no vignette, no gradient across the frame, no baked ambient occlusion in the corners and crevices, no light falloff towards the edges -- an uneven frame cannot tile, because its bright side would meet its dark side at every seam.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, realistic material, real surface wear and staining. Not stylised, not cartoon, not a 3D render preview, not a tiled collage of separate photographs, not a pattern illustration.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

name: Patchy Grass Ground Tile
nameTh: พื้นหญ้าและดิน
notes: One flat quad, 8 x 8 m, lying in the ground plane at y=0 -- two triangles, one geometry, one draw call, one PBR material, and nothing else. There are no grass cards, no billboards and no alpha-tested blades: the grass is painted into the albedo with its clumping carried by the normal and AO maps, seen from standing eye height and above, which is the only way a ground cover fits this kit's budget. That is a deliberate limitation and it means the tile reads correctly from a walking camera and poorly from a camera lying on it. This is a member of the kit's ground-surface tile set: every tile in that set is 8 x 8 m, sits at y=0, uses pivot base-center and snaps on the kit's 8 m grid, so it butts flush against any other ground tile and against the asphalt road tiles, and the raised Concrete Sidewalk Strip (2.0 m wide, 0.15 m tall) sits alongside as a separate object. It is categorised as a building-part rather than as vegetation because it is a ground tile in that modular set and shares its whole contract; the vegetation category's size prior tops out around 3 m and describes potted plants and shrubs, which this is not. Coarse patchy grass worn through to red earth is the surface of Thai verges, temple and school grounds, park lawns, futsal-pitch surrounds and the strip between a soi and a wall -- always partly bare, because tropical lawn does not survive being walked on. Because the cover is irregular with no direction, it is fully FOUR-way rotationally symmetric and drops in at any of four orientations, which matters here because a large lawn is where a visible repeat shows worst. The first thing to check on the generated texture is that no distinctive bare patch or tuft appears twice across a seam. Budget overridden explicitly to 2 triangles / 1 draw call / 1 material / 1 unique geometry instead of the hero2x its 8 m footprint would derive: footprint drives the class, but there is no geometry here to spend a class budget on. No destruction groups: a ground tile is static level geometry, not a breakable.
